We have never stayed in accommodation that was this dirty. The location itself is beautiful, and thankfully, the air conditioning worked.

Only Mimi speaks English; unfortunately, no one else does. Whenever we wanted to order something, we had to use hand gestures and try to explain what we wanted. The food is not recommended either, so we ended up walking to a resort further down the beach to eat.

There were insects everywhere in our room, including biting ants, mosquitoes, and spiders. The bathroom had clumps of hair left behind by previous guests, and judging by the overall condition of the room, it was clear that it had not been properly cleaned.

The water smelled strongly of sewage, which was extremely unpleasant.

The beach loungers are made of bare wood with no cushions, making them very uncomfortable to lie on.

Overall, this place is far too expensive for what you get. The property is in serious need of renovation and, in our opinion, should either be properly renovated or closed until it meets basic standards.

We also did not feel particularly welcomed by the staff. Most of the time, the staff were either sleeping in the hammocks or sitting on their phones. If you decide to stay here, be prepared for very limited English communication and a lack of service.

The location is beautiful, and the air conditioning worked, but unfortunately, those are the only positives we can mention. For the price, we expected much more.

Notre séjour au Pir Perhentian a malheureusement été une grande déception.
L’hôtel possède pourtant un véritable atout : une très belle plage privatisée, dans un cadre magnifique.
Cependant, la qualité de la chambre et surtout son niveau de propreté sont très loin de ce que nous pouvions attendre.
Dès notre arrivée, nous avons été confrontés à une forte odeur nauséabonde et d´égoût dans la salle de bain, qui était par ailleurs loin d’être propre. La vitre n’était visiblement pas nettoyée et l’ensemble donnait une impression générale de manque d’entretien.
Les serviettes fournies étaient également sales et présentaient des taches jaunes, ce qui est particulièrement décevant et peu acceptable pour un établissement hôtelier.
Mais le plus désagréable a été de retrouver des cafards dans la chambre pendant la nuit à 4h du matin, dont un qui est apparu sur notre table de chevet alors que nous dormions. Ce genre de situation est particulièrement stressant et nous a empêchés de par ailleurs de dormir sereinement mais de profiter pleinement de la fin de notre séjour. Je ne me suis sentie vraiment pas à l’aise du tout dans notre chambre et ne prenais aucun plaisir à y être dedans ma seule envie était d’en sortir et une hâte que le séjour ce termine. Nous avons conclue que ça ne servait à rien de se plaindre à la réception au vu de tout les précédents avis négatifs sur plusieurs années et que rien avait changer ou qu’aucun remboursement n’avait été fait.

The beach was absolutely breathtaking crystal-clear turquoise water, incredibly clean surroundings, and beautiful white sand that sparkles under the sunshine. It felt like a little piece of paradise!

De kwaliteit van het resort is echter matig. Huisjes zijn wat verouderd en wij hadden meerdere avonden kakkerlakken op bezoek. Wij verbleven 5 nachten, geen enkele keer is de WC en douche schoongemaakt (wel dagelijks huisje vegen, bed opmaken, nieuwe handdoeken en WC rollen aanvullen). Personeel was matig behulpzaam bij vragen en het restaurant was redelijk van kwaliteit.

In een oerwoud horen dieren en dat daarmee veranen, apen, gekko's en eekhoorns rondlopen is leuk. We hebben daarvan genoten.

Betaling kan overigens gewoon met je creditcard (bij vrijwel alle restaurants op het eiland). Bootservice naar de andere stranden of Kecil kan snel en eenvoudig (deze wel contant betalen). Tip: wil je wijn drinken: neem deze mee vanaf de vaste wal.

I want to be fair. Perhaps this would have been a wonderful experience for a young family, if they are OK with very “rustic” accommodations. We are not that young family. We paid $800 ringgit per night for what we believed would be at least an adequate resort (in Kuala Lumpur, that same $800 would have more than paid for a suite in a 5-star hotel). Our expectations were not super high, since we understood that we were paying for an experience on a private island. Just clean and comfortable. Unfortunately, we got neither. Our room, #208 had a broken front door that only opened 1/3 of the way, scraping across the floor and then stopping. There were deep gouges and white paint all over the floor, which let us know this issue is ongoing. At first glance, the room looked clean (and bedding was fresh), but on further inspection we could see that only surface cleaning has ever been done. The doors were filthy, mold stains on walls, absolute filth in the pipes and shower drain and air conditioning filters. Dirty, streaked mirrors. Also, the king size bed was hard as a rock - extremely uncomfortable with a poor quality mattress. We paid an extra $100 ringgit for an “extra bed” which was just a cot - a plastic mattress. Food at PIR is bad and obscenely expensive. Piles of trash behind convenience stores and coffee shops. And overall, a deeply unpleasant sewage smell in our room and permeating the island. The good: beach is absolutely lovely. Water is crystal clear, sand is white. No trash on the beach (they hide trash behind businesses, but it’s obvious as it stinks and attracts rodents). It was a wonderful experience to swim with colorful tropical fish. That was the one and only thing I appreciated about this overpriced and horrifically maintained island.

Beautiful resort with great potential, but service needs improvement – 7.5/10||We spent a week at this Marriott resort and overall had a very enjoyable stay. The property is beautiful, our accommodation was extremely comfortable, the views were wonderful, and we really appreciated our  villa with a private pool.||Breakfast was definitely one of the highlights — excellent variety and quality, especially the freshly! |A special mention must go to Zafirah, our Villa Host, who was absolutely wonderful: kind, attentive, always available and genuinely interested in making our stay special. We also really appreciated the lovely touches for our wedding anniversary.||That said, for a 5-star Marriott resort at this price level, there are some areas that really need improvement.||The biggest issue for us was the restaurant service. Although the staff were always friendly, service was consistently very slow and dishes for the same table rarely arrived together. On several occasions, one of us had almost finished eating before the other person’s meal arrived.|There were also some surprising operational issues. The beach bar was out of basic items, including water, for several days, which is difficult to understand at a 5-star tropical resort.||The management of sunbeds around the pool also needs attention. Guests reserve them early with towels and belongings and sometimes do not appear until hours later. We were told there is a 15–20 minute policy for unattended sunbeds, but unfortunately we never saw it being enforced.||Finally, the arrival experience could be much more polished. First impressions matter, and the transfer/check-in process did not feel particularly premium or aligned with what we expected from a resort of this category.||Overall, we would rate our experience 7.5/10. There is a lot to love here: beautiful surroundings, excellent accommodation, a great breakfast and some genuinely lovely staff. However, at this price point, the consistency of the service needs to match the quality of the resort itself.||With better restaurant coordination, attention to basic stock management, enforcement of pool policies and a more refined arrival experience, this could very easily become a 9/10 resort.

Quel gâchis alors que le potentiel est là  et que le site est magnifique !
Les chambres : globalement sales , la sdb délabrée, le ménage (vu)  est fait (en 5')  avec une serviette de plage sans produits d'entretien (ceci explique cela), les équipements cassés ou non entretenus. Les abords sont sales et ns avons fini par ramasser ce qui traînait autour de la chambre.
L'alimentation : allez manger dans l'hôtel à côté ! Les bacs ne sont pas remplis en continu, il faut compter 30'. Nous avons payé un buffet (×3) et il n'y avait qu'un bac de riz et un bac de viande, les 10 autres étaient vides a 19h30. Au bout de 40' nous sommes partis, le ventre quasi vide.... l'environnement est egalement sale et pas engageant.

La direction avertie s'est excusée et a envoyé une équipe faire un ménage complet. C'est gentil, mais les autres jours : retour aux habitudes.

Tout cela a un peu gâché notre sejour (4jours) qui a été sauvé par le restaurant d'à côté et par les fonds sous-marin magnifiques.

C'est bien dommage car le site a du potentiel, il manque juste un vrai management hôtelier : vérifier la qualité du ménage, tenir la zone de restauration propre, réachalander le buffet en continu et vérifier les abords du site pour enlever les déchets qui l'encombre.

Je suis très très très mitigée sur cet hôtel.

La plage est terriblement belle et l’hôtel terriblement vétuste. Je suis passée de l’ébahissement au dégoût tout au long de mon séjour.

La première certitude c’est qu’en séjournant là, il faut être très très à l’aise avec la faune: jeckos, lézards, fourmis, sauterelles, écureuils qui ressemblent à des rats, varans et même des varans malais. Dans la chambre, il y a tout de même une mise en garde contre toute cette faune et également contre des serpents. Sincèrement, nous n’en avons pas vu. Mais toutes ces bêtes sont omniprésentes. Donc j’ai passé un séjour en état d’alerte maximum 🤣

Ensuite, la chambre est crade au possible, elle sent les égouts et le linge de lit et de bain est… piteux. Troué, taché, jaune… j’ai mis des photos mais l’insalubrité générale de l’hôtel est indescriptible. Les transats à la plage sont des planches en bois sans matelas et il n’y a pas de parasols. Si vous vous mettez sous les palmiers, prenez garde aux écureuils qui en ont terrifié certains.
Pour finir, le petit déjeuner est très sommaire, le café indéfinissable: noir pétrole mais absolument aucun goût de café. Le resto du soir était sincèrement correct. Il n’y a rien à faire le soir, prévoyez un IPad et une connexion 4/5G qui fonctionne très bien. Il n’y a pas de wifi.

Quant à la plage… waouh! La plus belle de Perhentian. On a nagé quotidiennement avec des raies, des tortues, des bébés requins etc

Il y a plein de gens qui viennent à la journée (c’est le défilé des bateaux par contre) et je me demande si ce n’est pas ce qu’il faut faire en réalité. Bref.

Aussi je ne déconseillerais pas d’y aller vu la magie de la plage mais d’y aller en connaissance de cause et en payant le bon prix car moi, j’ai payé sur Agoda/Booking plus de 300€ la nuit et à ce prix là, c’est sincèrement du vol manifeste.

We stayed here for two nights with my husband to celebrate our wedding anniversary, and everything was absolutely perfect! The location is incredible, with a private beach that is among the most beautiful I have seen in Malaysia (and honestly… anywhere else too). The staff were incredibly kind, welcoming and always happy to help. Our room was wonderful, with a breathtaking view. The package also included several activities that we really enjoyed, such as snorkeling with turtles and kayaking. We were also incredibly lucky to take part in a turtle hatchling release, supporting SEATRUE, an organization dedicated to protecting these beautiful animals. It was a truly emotional and unforgettable experience. The food at the restaurant was also very good, and breakfast was excellent and plentiful.
There is also the opportunity to join yoga classes, either on the beach in the morning or in the dedicated yoga space overlooking the sea. Our instructor, Huril, was incredibly kind and very knowledgeable. The classes were both relaxing and enjoyable, but also challenging in the best possible way! I highly recommend staying at this resort and truly hope to be able to come back in the future!

Abbiamo passato in questo resort 5 giorni e 4 notti. Per iniziare devo dire che abbiamo sognato le isole perenthian per mesi, e devo dire che non deludono le aspettative, sono un paradiso incontaminata! Siamo però partiti un pò scoraggiati dalle recensioni delle varie strutture e dopo un annetto di ricerca conveniamo nel prenotare al PIR camera beach front. Capitolo posizione: sicuramente la spiaggia piu bella di tutte e due le isole, la spiaggia si trova a Besar(isola grande), posizione eccellente, turtle point a 50 m dalla riva. Tutti i giorni abbiamo fatto il bagno in mezzo a pesci di ogni specie,  razze e tanti squaletti pinna nera che venivano regolarmente a trovarci, sensazione meravigliosa! Capitolo camera: la camera beach front è sicuramente la migliore del resort,  abbiamo scelto il pacchetto colazione inclusa, la camera è in legno, sicuramente no  di lusso ma direi che le assegnerei 3 stelle. Comunque dispone di questa balconata fronte mare, ogni mattina ci siamo svegliati con il rumore del mare praticamente a 30 secondi di distanza da noi. Camera in sostanza pulita, ovviamente bisogna tenere presente che si è su un isola abbastanza selvaggia  in malesia. Capitolo servizi; i ragazzi che lavorano al PIR sono tutti gentilissimi e cordiali, sicuramente metterei piu lettini sulla spiaggia e magari una tipologia piu comoda, ma che te ne fai dei lettini quando hai quella sabbia paradisiaca? Capitolo cibo: la colazione del PIR era abbastanza fornita con una buona scelta internazionale e soprattutto asiatica. Conclusioni: la nostra esperienza estate piu che positiva! Ovviamente bisogna tenere conto che si è su un isola selvaggia, con un mare da sogno che sicuramente non ha niente da invidiare a posti come le Maldive. Inutile cercare una servizio 5 stelle, qui si viene per distaccarsi dal mondo! Lo consiglio vivamente a chi vuole immergersi in questo paradiso.

Magnifica esperienza, isola spettacolare con ottima ospitalità. Il Resort è un po datato ma offre quella familiarità che spesso si perde in strutture nuove. Bella la filosofia dietro alla preservazione dell’isola.

Il taaras si trova in una baia incantevole, acqua cristallina e sabbia bianca dove è facile incontrare pesci colorati tartarughe e piccoli squali innocui. Per il resto la struttura è bella ma a mio avviso non all'altezza di un 5 stelle. La cucina è si ampia, ma non così internazionale come dicono.i sapori sono prevalentemente asiatici. Il personale è molto cordiale e gentile, i bungalow in legno sono molto belli. Tra le varie attività organizzano le escursioni li davanti alla spiaggia, che sinceramente sono facilmente raggiungibili in autonomia con una canoa a costo zero. La sera non c'è molto movimento, un pò di musica live che però termina presto. Nel complesso un bellissimo posto che però si fa pagare e non poco.

Ho trascorso una settimana in questo paradiso terrestre e ci ho lasciato il cuore veramente. Partiamo dall’aspetto principale della struttura: LA POSIZIONE! Il PIR, credetemi, si adagia sulla spiaggia più bella delle Perhentian! Sabbia corallina, accecante! Un mare, io che ci sn stato lo confermo, che nulla ha da invidiare alle Maldive! Se venite qui non avete bisogno di escursioni! Il mare di fronte a voi vi regalerà uscite di snorkelling per vedere tartarughe, squaletti pinna nera, mante grigie, pesci pagliaccio…e, se siete particolarmente fortunati come lo sono stato io, il pesce Napoleone!
La colazione è asiatica e occidentale con una stazione per le uova. Consiglio di valutarla. Il ristorante sono molto lenti. Io ho sempre preso o riso o carne: si sa noi italiani siamo un po’ complicati! Non c’è alcuna possibilità di alcol! Se siete in astinenza andate a quelli vicini: al PIR nessuna chance. Le camere sono comode e spaziose. L’AC funziona bene. Le pulizie sono scarse e nn c’è acqua calda…ma nn è mai stato un problema! Il WiFi funziona solo alla reception e male: se dovete aggiornare il OS o grandi GB andate al mattino presto e/o la sera tardi…
Certo…un po’ di adattamento in valigia con te devi portarlo ma questo mare dí ricompenserà con gli interessi!
Escursioni consiglio Redang: è sì la più costosa ma Redang vale la pena credetemi!
Kecil: andate una sera alla sua gemellina su long beach. Sedetevi su uno dei tanti locali e scegliete il pesce che volete mangiare. Poi andate a vedervi lo spettacolo del fuoco!

Chambre sale ( telecde clim couverte de marques de doigts, draps grisâtres et mal odorants dito les serviettes usagers, on ne voit plus à travers le parement verre de la douche, blattes dans la douche, abattant de wc non stable, rat aperçu sur les charpentes de l’espace restauration, restaurant pas terrible du tout, personnel plus intéressé par leur smartphone que par leur boulot, espace à potentiel mais pas d’entretien. Incredible potential - very disappointing execution. If I start with the positives, the resort is situated on an incredible beach, crystal clear sea with a simple water taxi system that can take you to a number of other beautiful locations around the island. The resort itself would be best described as neglected. Full of promise and really disappointing delivery as the rooms are less than clean, with very dated bathrooms and evidence of bed bugs that had once infested the room. The rooms are very close to the beach, making the views from the balcony a bit of a bonus. The facilities in the resort were pretty rubbish to be honest, a dirty unused pool, empty games room, one set of badminton rackets for the entire hotel to share, a karaoke room that you can pay extra to use, absolutely no daytime/evening entertainment and breakfast/dinner service that was quite shocking. I wouldn’t mind having limited service but the resort advertises WiFi, then informs you on arrival that it is only available in reception - a place you probably want to avoid as much as possible. One of the reasons to travel to SE Asia is for the food, then you are met with a cold, stale selection of buffet food. The BBQ buffet somehow doubles the price of the service whilst serving much of the same food but warmed on the grill before service. I think the lowlight of the resort however has to be the service from the reception team. The ladies appeared frankly irritated during any interaction and would best be described as less than welcoming. The laundry service was not running due to “bad water”, despite it being promoted on the room information - not sure if this was a short term or long term issue they were having.

I was unfortunate enough to suffer from a series of lacerations on my hand from a quite bizarre needlefish attack, this led to significant bleeding. The receptionists were completely uninterested in helping me, nor did they demonstrate any empathy as I bled out in reception. I was lucky enough that a paramedic guest was checking in at that time and assisted me. Bizarrely, the receptionists weren’t even enthusiastic about having the blood cleaned from the floor and it dried/remained there for the final day of our stay. Their service peaked when they asked us to return the spare roll of toilet paper that we had been using to help clean up some of the spilled blood - there is no telling what they would have wanted to do with it had we obliged, which we did not.

It is hard to describe why, but the resort feels overstaffed without ever having anyone available that can help you with any of your needs. I am yet to work out why staff were distributed in a way that felt as though they were able to enjoy each others company as opposed to meeting the needs of guests. One man in the only functioning coffee shop battled away as three members of staff sat in the other cafe unable to serve due to a lack of beans. The collection of slackers appeared offended when I proposed that one of them perhaps join him in his struggle or fetch some of his beans (I even offered to undertake this 5 minute walk for them) so they might be able to serve to share the burden - their response made me feel stupid for thinking out loud.

To summarise, if spending time on a beautiful beach supplemented by poorly maintained facilities, limited selection of gross food and staff that don’t care about you is not your thing, give this place a miss!

Par où commencer….
Nous avons été placé dans la chambre 228 qui était séparée et mitoyenne avec la chambre 227. Les murs étaient tellement fins que l’on était ravis d’entendre toutes les joies et peines de la famille d’à côté… Mais le principal problème est l’entretien du bungalow. Entre les tâches d’humidité, l’odeur des canalisations dans la salle de bains, l’eau jaunâtre qui sort du robinet et de la douche, les infestations de termites, etc., on sent que le principal but des gérants n’est pas de faire passer un bon séjour aux voyageurs. Alors oui le ménage est effectué (rapidement) tout les jours et l’équipe essaye de régler les problèmes mais je pense que la priorité est à mettre dans un petit coup de neuf. Le petit déjeuner est ok sans plus, le resort est équipé de certains services agréables, mais le véritable point fort est la localisation. Il est situé sur la plus belles plage de l’île où l’on peut croiser requins, raies et tortues à 5 mètres du rivage. Mais je pense que la gérance se base uniquement là dessus pour faire valoir des prix aussi élevés car l’hôtel en lui-même ne les mérite vraiment pas! En résumé, je ne sais pas si je peux vous conseiller ce logement car je pense que cela est plus agréable et pourrait revenir moins cher de loger ailleurs sur l’île et de profiter de leur plage en prenant des bateaux taxis.
Don’t expect much luxury. The rooms are old, but fine if your expectations are low. There is a nice swimming area and the beaches are stunning.

La ubicación es espectacular, pero es lo único que se salva. El estado del resort y el nivel de mantenimiento son, sencillamente, inaceptables. Este es, de largo, el peor sitio donde me he alojado, y he viajado bastante.

Para empezar, la limpieza es totalmente inexistente. Durante toda la estancia (seis días) se limitaron a cambiar las toallas y a poner botellas de agua. No limpiaron la habitación ni el cuarto de baño, ni cambiaron las sábanas. Un día olvidaron reponer el papel higiénico (tuve que ir a pedirlo a recepción); otro, vaciar la papelera y un tercer día, directamente no pasaron a "limpiar" la habitación: tuvimos que reclamarlo también.

Las instalaciones están muy deterioradas. El mobiliario es viejo, desgastado y sucio, los cristales están llenos de suciedad, la ducha necesita una renovación urgente y varios elementos de la habitación no funcionan correctamente. Además, carece de lo más básico: no hay armario ni cajones donde guardar la ropa. Por otro lado, nos encontramos dos cucarachas en el cuarto de baño. Que esto ocurra en un alojamiento que cobra estos precios es sencillamente inaceptable.

Respecto a la comida del restaurante, es cara y de bajísima calidad. El desayuno, además de escaso, ofrece una variedad mínima y todos los productos están destapados, en un sitio donde moscas y mosquitos campan a sus anchas.

Es una pena que un lugar con una ubicación tan privilegiada esté tan mal gestionado. A mí no me quedó más remedio que hacer la reserva en este sitio porque, por circunstancias, miré los alojamientos tarde y solo quedaba una habitación en este. Por eso, recomiendo encarecidamente a quien tenga pensado pasar unos días en Perhentian que reserve con mucha antelación para que no le ocurra lo mismo que a nosotr@s. Sería una lástima que lo que puede ser una  experiencia inolvidable en unas playas paradisíacas se convierta en inolvidable por motivos muy distintos.

The hotel itself is overpriced and they charge extortionate prices for essentials like water and coffee. A bottle of water costs 10MYR and a coffee 20MYR, while in George Town I paid just 2MYR for both. After sun in the shop is 39MYR, something you could get for less than half of that usually.

The sun loungers are wooden with no comfort. The beach is overcrowded during the day due to boat trips to see the turtles, which completely ruins the experience.

Breakfast is average, with the best part being the fresh eggs. However, you have to queue and wait as the chef can only prepare two at a time.  If you arrive near closing time, there’s no food left.  Ants and flies are also a problem.

I arrived without any running water and wasn’t warned beforehand or apologised to. The water outage lasted longer than expected with no communication. The WiFi is only available in the main area and is poor quality.

The reception and restaurant staff were unfriendly. I wasn’t informed about the breakfast time and had to carry my heavy bags up several flights of stairs to my room. This is far from what I would expect for the price.

The bed was comfortable, the room was clean and the beach views were great. But I’d strongly recommend staying somewhere else and coming to this beach to visit.

Nous avons réservé cet hôtel car il possédait l’une des plus belles plages des îles Perhentian. Nous savions à l’avance que les logements sur les îles ne sont généralement pas exceptionnels. Malheureusement, nous nous sommes dit qu’en choisissant un hôtel plus cher, nous aurions au moins un logement convenable. Dès notre arrivée, nous avons été surpris par la saleté de la chambre. Elle n’était pas propre : il y avait des cheveux dans la salle de bain, la vitre de la douche était très sale et semblait ne jamais avoir été nettoyée, le sol n’avait pas été balayé et la poussière n’avait pas été faite non plus. Nous avions demandé une chambre avec deux lits doubles, mais nous avons eu deux lits simples. Après notre réclamation, une employée nous a proposé une autre chambre avec un lit double, mais avec une vue vraiment peu agréable. Nous avons donc préféré rester dans la chambre initiale. Concernant le ménage quotidien, la salle de bain n’a jamais été lavée correctement, les lits étaient faits à moitié et le balcon n’était jamais nettoyé. J’ai été extrêmement surprise par ce manque d’entretien. J’ai également fait une intoxication alimentaire pendant deux jours après avoir mangé de la pastèque. J’ai cru mourir tellement j’ai été malade, donc faites attention. Ne vous fiez pas au prix. Choisissez plutôt un établissement convenable et bien entretenu. Les autres hôtels aux alentours semblent offrir une qualité similaire, voire meilleure, pour le prix qu’ils proposent.

Beautiful location for a relaxing few days. Our garden room was very spacious, clean and comfortable, stocked with drinks and toiletteries. I came here on my company trips and everything is not worth being a 5* hotel. The buffet has limited choices and all of them are average at best. I understand being a 5* hotel they have to charge it at higher price, especially when they trying to earn money off foreigners. But the up charge on any of the activities are too much. 200rm for 1hour of karaoke is just out right scam. Nous tenons également à remercier Nadia, à la réception, qui nous a très bien accompagnés tout au long de notre séjour. Elle s’est montrée très efficace et disponible pour répondre à toutes nos demandes, que ce soit en personne ou sur WhatsApp.||Le petit déjeuner était excellent, avec une mention spéciale pour le stand de roti canai, que nous avons beaucoup apprécié. La plage de l’hôtel est également magnifique, avec une eau d’un bleu cristallin, ce qui rend le cadre particulièrement agréable.||Nous avons toutefois été surpris par certains aspects de l’hôtel. Le rapport qualité-prix nous a semblé décevant, le tarif étant assez élevé pour un établissement qui paraît quelque peu vieillissant et qui mériterait plusieurs améliorations, notamment au niveau de la literie. Il s’agit du principal point négatif pour un hôtel de cette catégorie et à ce prix : nous nous réveillions le matin avec le dos complètement douloureux en raison de la qualité du matelas.||Nous avons également régulièrement constaté des odeurs de remontées d’égout dans la salle de bain. Par ailleurs, nous avons été surpris de devoir payer pour les masques et les tubas de snorkeling après deux heures d’utilisation. Au vu du prix de l’hôtel, ce matériel devrait être prêté gratuitement, d’autant que les clients viennent notamment pour profiter de la magnifique plage proposée par l’établissement.||Dans l’ensemble, nous avons passé un très bon séjour au Taaras et avons particulièrement apprécié son cadre exceptionnel, sa plage et la gentillesse de son personnel. L’hôtel mérite le détour, même si certaines améliorations permettraient de rendre l’expérience encore plus agréable.

We stayed for three nights as a family of four and appreciated being upgraded to a larger two-bedroom Cliff Bay Suite. It was spacious and comfortable, and the complimentary minibar on arrival was a nice touch.

The resort’s greatest strength is undoubtedly its setting: a truly beautiful beach, clear water and a sheltered bay. Snorkelling with turtles was one of the highlights of our stay. We also paid to visit the turtle conservation centre, where our children learned about conservation and, under close supervision, carefully helped uncover baby turtles from the sand. It was a meaningful and memorable experience.

The complimentary entertainment lounge—with foosball, pool, table tennis, mahjong and carrom—was another good feature for families. Some staff were genuinely warm, friendly and full of smiles, particularly at ASEAN All Day Dining. The breakfast buffet itself, however, had a surprisingly limited spread for a five-star resort.

Unfortunately, service elsewhere was inconsistent. Some buggy drivers appeared uninterested, and we observed one using his phone while driving, which was a genuine safety concern. Drinks ordered from the bar never arrived, while indoor dining involved long waits and follow-up calls. The repeated lapses across different departments suggested wider issues with training, supervision and internal communication rather than a single isolated incident.

Food and drinks were expensive, yet the quality and service did not consistently justify the prices. The excursions were also costly, although the turtle conservation visit was a worthwhile exception. The kids’ club felt basic and underwhelming for a family resort at this price point. While our upgraded suite was spacious, the room and several other areas felt dated and overdue for refurbishment.

We also found it odd that sustainability videos from 2020 were still being shown without more recent updates. Our conservation-centre visit showed that at least some valuable work continues, but relying on six-year-old material leaves guests wondering about the progress of the resort’s other initiatives. The beach and water remain beautiful, although they did not always appear quite as pristine as in the older footage.

The Taaras has the ingredients to be exceptional: an extraordinary beach, memorable wildlife experiences, spacious accommodation and clear international appeal, including among the many Italian visitors we encountered. However, a five-star experience must also include consistently attentive service, safe practices, well-maintained facilities, good food and value for money. On those measures, our stay felt closer to a four-star experience despite luxury-level prices.

As Malaysian guests, we genuinely wanted to support and recommend a local resort attracting visitors from around the world. That is why this was more disappointing than upsetting. With better training, coordination, maintenance and value, The Taaras could be outstanding. Based on our experience and the price paid, however, we would find it difficult to recommend it in its present form.

We booked our stay through an agent at Perhentian Island Resort, which is already notably more expensive than other nearby hotels. Unfortunately, the arrival and check-in experience left much to be scenery.

Upon arriving at the jetty around 11:00 am, we were greeted with a complete lack of guidance or a proper welcome. There were no signs or staff directing us, so we had to walk blindly from the jetty to find the reception counter on our own.

Our travel agent's itinerary, noted that check-in could be as early as 12:00 pm (international check-in time). However, hotel staff told us we had to wait until 3:00 pm for our seaview chalet. We left our bags in the luggage room and wandered the beach to pass the time. Even after pushing our luck, the receptionist wouldn't hand over the keys until 2:00 pm.

The chalet was well air-conditioned, and basic amenities were provided for our 3-day stay. We were also very fortunate to have a continuous water supply despite receiving a letter about a potential water disruption.

The toilet had a bit of a smell. Additionally, the two power outlets next to the mirror were broken, forcing us to share the working plug with the kettle.

The provided mugs and glass cups were visibly dirty. We had to physically bring them back to reception to demand a clean replacement.

Also, make sure to pack plenty of insect repellent as the mosquitoes right outside the rooms are relentless!

The beach itself is absolutely gorgeous, clean, and crystal clear so no complaints there! You can easily spot baby blacktip reef sharks, stingrays, and schools of fish right by the shore.

Because this beach doubles as a major island snorkeling point, it gets quite noisy when all the tour boats park close to the sand. It is also incredibly frustrating to find an open beach chair to place your belongings, as families tend to hog and hoard them all day.

We had the full breakfast, lunch, and dinner buffet during our stay. The food definitely needs improvement. Many of the dishes didn't taste very good or were heavily over-salted. On top of that, there was a major issue with flies landing on the buffet spreads; even though the resort installed those little spinning fan tools to shoo them away, they weren't very effective.

The beach and natural marine life are breathtaking, but for the premium price tag, the resort desperately needs to step up its service, room maintenance, and buffet quality.

The Verdict: Stay somewhere else and just visit this beach.
Perhentian Island Resort sits on what is arguably the most breathtaking, crystal-clear stretch of white sand and turtle-snorkeling reef on the entire island. However, the resort itself is a massive letdown. You are paying a premium price for a property that feels neglected, dated, and poorly managed.

The Bad: The rooms are in desperate need of a renovation—expect septic tank smell from poorly maintained toilets, musty smell, stained linens, plumbing issues, in room safe that does not work , and zero Wi-Fi or poor phone signal in the chalets. - we changed rooms and had the same issues. The included buffet breakfast is incredibly basic and lacks quality and cleanliness (flies on food) while the overall resort infrastructure struggled with basic utilities like running water. (We could not shower, flush, or wash hands at one point our stay). 2 rooms per chalet have very thin walls, so expect smelling and hearing your neighbour if they have a conversation, or smoke a cigarette.

The Good: The location is a 10/10. The water is pristine, and you can literally swim out from the shore to snorkel with sea turtles and fish without needing a boat tour.

Final Thoughts and recommendations: Do not look at the booking photos; they do not reflect the current run-down state of the rooms and common areas. Save yourself the frustration: book a better-maintained hotel nearby for a comfortable night's sleep, and just take a water taxi over to this beach during the day to enjoy the spectacular nature.

Recommend to upgrade at least on plumbing and ventilation infrastructures, and management to have goals to realise the full potential of this wonderful location.

La baia privata è semplicemente spettacolare: acqua cristallina, sabbia bianca e un’atmosfera rilassante che rende questo luogo un vero paradiso. Il resort offre tantissime attività, dal kayak agli sport acquatici, fino a un dive center ben organizzato per chi desidera esplorare i magnifici fondali della zona.

Anche la proposta gastronomica è molto completa, con la possibilità di scegliere tra buffet e ristoranti à la carte, senza dover uscire dal resort. Essendo praticamente l’intero complesso dell’isola, si trova davvero tutto ciò di cui si può avere bisogno.

Personale disponibile. L’unico piccolo appunto è che, a tratti, il servizio è sembrato un po’ “robotizzato”, molto formale e meno spontaneo rispetto ad altri resort che abbiamo visitato.

Nel complesso è una destinazione che consigliamo assolutamente a chi cerca mare da cartolina, relax, immersioni e comfort in un contesto esclusivo. Un soggiorno che ricorderemo con grande piacere.

Location spettacolare, servizio incredibile. Camerieri e chef super attenti e cordiali. Mia moglie è celiaca e ha potuto assaggiare tutti i piatti locali tipici e asiatici grazie alla cura e all'attenzione del maitre Saifoo e dello chef Affandi.

For our recent getaway, we booked The Taaras, supposedly the best hotel on Redang Island. With that reputation and the price tag, we arrived expecting a little bit of wow.

Arrival:
The welcome was pretty much “hey you made it.”  . We were served a welcome drink that tasted as if the juice concentrate was more of a suggestion than an ingredient.

We arrived way too early and our room wasn’t ready for early check-in, so we were then told to leave our bags on the floor by the stairs. For a resort charging these rates, I assumed a proper luggage area might have made it into the budget, but apparently not- the staircase floor is the luggage lounge.

We left our bags to enjoy the beach, and we can confirm this is where The Taaras absolutely earns its reputation.

The beach:
The beach is breathtaking. Hands down, the most beautiful beach on Redang Island. The sand is incredibly white, the water is crystal clear, and the scenery is spectacular. If the welcome drink was 99% water and 1% juice, at least the water at the beach was actually impressive.

The room:
Our Bay View room was amazing. A big thank you to the hotel management for assigning us Room 251. The room was perfect, and the view of the beach was spectacular. We loved the slice of cake and the beautiful anniversary message displayed on the screen- though we had to turn on the TV to see it. It was a thoughtful touch.

Breakfast at Asian Dining restaurant:
Breakfast had a good spread, although most of the food sat comfortably in the moderately good category. The croissant was soft, and limp. The roti canai was fine, even though i think a splash of sambal would take it up a notch.

We ordered iced chocolate drinks, which arrived as a joke. Between this and the welcome drink, I strongly suspect the beverage department is either terrified of flavour or operating under extremely strict flavor rationing. Perhaps a little more training in beverage making?

Recreation Center:
We made good use of the Sports and Recreation Center. Renting equipment such as the canoes, snorkelling gear and an underwater camera was easy, and returning everything was straightforward. The staff were extremely helpful, especially Kak Husni, who made things simple for us

The only issue though was transferring the underwater camera files. We couldn’t transfer everything because the videos were large, despite averaging around two minutes each. If only the centre could temporarily upload the files to cloud storage and provide guests with a download link. That would save everyone from standing around watching a transfer progress bar move with the urgency of a sea cucumber.

Customer Service:
One thing that genuinely stood out was the customer service. The staff were consistently friendly and helpful, when approached, but some moments went beyond the usual resort service. A staff member helped attend to our minor wounds after a snorkelling activity, and we even saw another staff member helping a guest tie her hair. How lovely is that.

We had the pleasure of riding with Rafiq, one of the buggy drivers, who remembered us by our room number, so every trip between our room and the lobby was effortless. He shared helpful tips and was a pleasure to chat with.

Overall, The Taaras has an absolutely spectacular beach, beautiful views, excellent rooms and some genuinely wonderful staff. The natural setting does a lot of the heavy lifting.

They just have to work on the arrival experience, and beverage quality.

Abbiamo soggiornato al The Taaras Beach & Spa e, nel complesso, è stata un'esperienza molto positiva.

Il resort è bello, curato e rappresenta la migliore struttura dell'isola di Redang. Le Garden Suite sono ben tenute e, a mio parere, hanno una posizione decisamente più comoda rispetto alle camere vista mare, perché permettono di raggiungere facilmente spiaggia, piscina e ristoranti.

Il prezzo è sicuramente elevato rispetto a quanto viene offerto: personalmente lo considererei più vicino a un buon resort 4 stelle europeo che a un vero resort di lusso. Nonostante questo, resta comunque la scelta migliore sull'isola.

La colazione è ottima, molto varia e con ampia scelta. Il ristorante Asean, invece, non mi ha particolarmente convinta. Ho apprezzato il beach bar per la comodità e l'atmosfera, anche se la pizza è decisamente migliorabile. Suggerirei inoltre di ampliare le proposte vegetariane del ristorante the cove.

Il vero punto di forza è il servizio: ogni giorno lo staff contatta gli ospiti su WhatsApp per chiedere come sta andando il soggiorno ed è sempre rapido nel risolvere qualsiasi problema. Ho trovato molto piacevoli anche i piccoli dettagli, come i cioccolatini lasciati ogni sera in camera, il minibar rifornito quotidianamente, la lounge dedicata all'attesa all'aeroporto di Kuala Terengganu e la musica dal vivo durante l'aperitivo e la cena.

La pulizia è buona, la spiaggia è ben tenuta e la posizione è perfetta per raggiungere il punto di osservazione delle tartarughe. Lo snorkeling è molto bello, con la possibilità di noleggiare facilmente tutta l'attrezzatura necessaria. Un enorme valore aggiunto è poter assistere alla nidificazione delle tartarughe sulla spiaggia e, quando possibile, partecipare alla liberazione dei piccoli: un'esperienza davvero emozionante.

Ho trovato molto comodo anche avere il villaggio proprio accanto al resort, dove si può cenare nei ristoranti locali spendendo circa un terzo rispetto ai ristoranti dell'hotel e, spesso, mangiando anche meglio.

Il materasso è molto comodo, nella sala comune sono disponibili giochi per intrattenersi e il clima è stato perfetto: nonostante le previsioni indicassero pioggia continua, abbiamo avuto solo brevi acquazzoni notturni. Il mare è semplicemente il più caldo e azzurro che abbia mai visto e durante il soggiorno è possibile osservare tantissimi animali marini.

Ci sono però anche alcuni aspetti migliorabili. Le zanzare della sabbia sono numerosissime, anche all'interno delle camere: consiglio di portare un repellente davvero efficace. Alcune sdraio e tavolini sulla spiaggia avrebbero bisogno di una pulizia più accurata.

Non ho apprezzato la presenza costante dello yacht del proprietario ancorato nella baia, perché rovina un po' la vista naturale di questo luogo magnifico.

La nota più triste riguarda purtroppo la quantità di plastica e microplastiche presenti sia sulla spiaggia sia in mare. Il proprietario mostra con orgoglio i progetti di riqualificazione e pulizia, iniziativa davvero ammirevole, ma purtroppo basta fare pochi passi per trovare microplastiche, bottiglie, accendini e altri rifiuti. Mi sarebbe piaciuto trovare dei cestelli o dei sacchi messi a disposizione degli ospiti che desiderano dedicare un po' del loro tempo a ripulire questo paradiso.

Infine, avrei gradito un po' più di intrattenimento serale. A parte la piacevole musica dal vivo, le serate risultano piuttosto tranquille: una serata disco, un white party o qualche spettacolo aggiuntivo renderebbero l'esperienza ancora più completa.

Nel complesso consiglio il The Taaras Beach & Spa a chi cerca il mare più bello che si possa immaginare, un resort ben gestito e un servizio molto attento. Con qualche miglioramento e un rapporto qualità-prezzo più equilibrato potrebbe diventare davvero un punto di riferimento assoluto.

We stayed at The Taaras hoping for a relaxing family getaway, and while parts of it delivered, several avoidable issues took the shine off.

Room allocation: Before arriving, we specifically requested twin rooms in the same block, ideally close to reception, and were told this would be "accommodated." Despite the resort not being at full occupancy, we were placed in the garden view block furthest from reception — not the twins-together setup we'd asked for. Not the start we were hoping for.

Check-in: The check-in process itself felt underwhelming and rushed. We weren't given any orientation — no signage or directions to the beach, and no mention of the sandfly issue (more on that below) or the turtle release happening that same evening. We only found out about the turtle release from friendly staff down at the beach, and it ended up being a real highlight — but it shouldn't have been left to chance. It should also have been mentioned during check in that the hot water only works if you turn on the SWITCH for 15 minutes before taking a shower . as a result a poor cold first day shower experience with poor water pressure

Sandflies: This was our biggest issue. Nobody warned us about sandflies, and by the end of day one I'd been bitten around 25 times and my son closer to 50. The itching kept us both up most of the night. A simple heads-up at check-in (with repellent recommendations, or even repellent provided) would have made a huge difference.

Wifi: In-room wifi was patchy and unreliable throughout our stay.
The positives: The rooms themselves were genuinely luxurious and matched the price point. The beach is stunning — genuinely one of the best we've experienced — and the turtle release was a magical, unexpected bonus.

Spa: A real highlight of the trip. Glory's team massage was fantastic, and the traditional Taaras herbal bag massage was excellent — worth booking in advance. Glory herself was the first person we met who we could say embodied a true 5 star experience!

Staff: Mixed experience. The beach staff and spa team were warm and attentive. Reception, however, could use more training in guest service — better attention to pre-arrival requests and basic welcome information would go a long way, including information (and a basic leaflet for asking us to check amentiies via scannign a QR code - available we found AFTERWARDS)

In summary: Gorgeous location, excellent spa, but the resort needs to tighten up communication — from honoring room requests to warning guests about sandflies and letting them know about evening events like the turtle release.

A resort that is clearly in need of renovation

Berjaya Tioman Resort has, according to its own website, been around since 1985. That makes it 41 years old, and unfortunately, the age of the resort is also quite noticeable in some of the rooms.

Our room had an outdated and very firm bed, with the springs clearly noticeable. There were also quite a lot of ants in the room, as well as several issues with the finishing that, in our opinion, do not fit a hotel presenting itself as a luxury golf resort. The door was sticking when both opening and closing. The wooden bathroom door showed clear signs of wood rot and had been poorly repaired. Since there is no shower curtain, the door gets very wet after every shower, which certainly does not help. The sealant around the sink also looked very old and overdue for replacement.

The dining experience also felt rather dated. The menus at the restaurant and bars are old-fashioned laminated, folded A4 sheets, and several items listed on them were simply not available, including drinks such as Hoegaarden, Corona and Piña Colada. There is also very little communication about which restaurants and bars are open and when. For a resort of this size and standard, we would expect both the menus and the communication about the available dining options to be kept more up to date.

We also found that quite a lot of staff members were travelling back and forth around the resort on scooters. Given the size of the property, this is perhaps understandable, but it does take away somewhat from the peaceful resort atmosphere you might expect from a place like this.

Berjaya Tioman Resort proudly presents itself as the largest resort on Tioman. We are aware that the resort is currently undergoing renovations and that some room categories have already been updated. However, this does not fully address the issue from a guest's perspective. At present, it seems to be a matter of luck whether you receive a renovated room or one that is clearly in need of updating, while paying the same price. Until the renovation is completed across the resort, the experience can therefore vary considerably depending on the room you are allocated.

In our view, the remaining rooms should be brought up to current standards, with more consistency across the resort in terms of both room quality and overall presentation.

Fortunately, there are also positive aspects. The activities on offer are well organised, and the lobby staff are incredibly friendly, helpful and accommodating. When we arrived, we were initially given a room with two single beds, even though we had booked a double bed. After we raised this, it was resolved quickly and without any hassle.

In short: a beautifully located resort with friendly staff and well-organised activities, but the condition of some of the rooms and the dated overall presentation unfortunately seriously detract from the overall experience. A thorough renovation and update would certainly be worthwhile.

We had another wonderful experience at Kapalai Dive Resort. Our dive masters Ryan and Ardi were extremely friendly, knowledgeable, and excellent at spotting marine life. They were just as skilled at finding larger sea life as they were at discovering tiny macro creatures, which made every dive interesting. We saw a giant cuttlefish, a sleeping bamboo shark, and mimic octopi, amongst many other sea creatures! We had fantastic diving at Kapalai, Mabul, and the famous Sipadan Island, and really appreciated how attentive and experienced the dive team was.

The rest of the resort staff were also very friendly, welcoming, and helpful throughout our stay. The food was delicious and overall we felt the resort offered excellent value for such a unique experience.

One of the most fascinating things about Kapalai is the island itself. The tides completely change the scenery throughout the day. At high tide, the water can cover much of the island and you can have beautiful clear water directly underneath your chalet. At low tide, the water recedes, there may be little or no water beneath the chalet, and the exposed sand makes the island appear much larger. It was really interesting to watch the landscape transform with the tides.

Kapalai is a very special place and a fantastic choice for anyone who loves diving, marine life, and staying somewhere completely different from a typical resort. It's definitely worth the travel from Tawau airport. We would definitely recommend it!

Un cadre exceptionnel qui mériterait une expérience à la hauteur…

Nous avons séjourné au Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort pour notre lune de miel, et le lieu est tout simplement incroyable. L’hôtel est magnifique, parfaitement intégré à son environnement, avec des chambres typiques pleines de charme.
Nous avions une chambre côté corail, que nous recommandons vivement : la vue sur l’océan est exceptionnelle et, le soir, les tortues viennent littéralement vous dire bonne nuit 🐢
La localisation est absolument superbe.
Une petite attention avait été préparée dans notre chambre pour notre lune de miel, avec une jolie décoration, ce qui nous a beaucoup touchés.
Le service est également irréprochable : le personnel est adorable, souriant, disponible et toujours très agréable.

🤿 Un énorme coup de cœur pour le dive center !
Mention spéciale au dive center, qui est pour nous l’un des gros points forts du séjour. Et surtout, un immense merci à Linda, notre instructrice, qui nous a permis de découvrir la plongée et de partir à la découverte de plusieurs très beaux spots. Grâce à elle, nous avons vécu une expérience vraiment inoubliable 🤿❤️

Sous l’eau, il y a énormément de choses à observer, avec notamment de très grandes tortues, et en quantité ! 🐢 C’est un véritable plaisir de les voir évoluer dans leur environnement naturel.
En revanche, il ne faut pas venir ici en s’attendant à découvrir une immense barrière de corail intacte. La richesse marine reste néanmoins très intéressante et les rencontres avec les tortues valent vraiment le détour.

🚨Les points qui nous ont déçus…
Le principal point négatif concerne malheureusement une partie de la clientèle, notamment les groupes de touristes chinois. Leur comportement a parfois réellement gâché le charme et la tranquillité du lieu : cris, manque de respect envers le personnel et les autres clients, et comportements qui nous ont semblé peu adaptés à un établissement de ce standing.
Nous avons également eu le sentiment que l’organisation du resort était très tourné vers cette clientèle.
C’est vraiment dommage, car un cadre aussi exceptionnel mériterait une ambiance beaucoup plus calme et respectueuse.
Nous trouvons notamment dommage que l’hôtel réserve directement une part importante de ses chambres à des agences chinoises. Cela semble contribuer à une forte concentration de cette clientèle au sein du resort et, par conséquent, à l’ambiance parfois très bruyante et peu respectueuse que nous avons pu constater pendant notre séjour.

🍽️ Le buffet, un autre point à améliorer…
Nous savons que nous sommes dans un resort all-inclusive 3 étoiles et nous n’attendions évidemment pas de la gastronomie. Mais avec des produits simples, il serait tout à fait possible de proposer une cuisine beaucoup plus qualitative.
Nous avons trouvé beaucoup de produits industriels, ce qui est dommage, et relativement peu de spécialités malaisiennes. C’est particulièrement regrettable lorsque l’on vient de l’étranger et que l’on souhaite justement découvrir la cuisine locale. Là encore, nous avons parfois eu l’impression que le buffet était davantage adapté aux habitudes de la clientèle chinoise qu’à une clientèle internationale.

📍En résumé :
Le Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort pourrait vraiment avoir tout d’un 4 étoiles grâce à son cadre exceptionnel, ses chambres pleines de charme, sa localisation unique, la qualité de son personnel et surtout son excellent centre de plongée.
Malheureusement, certains choix concernant la clientèle accueillie et la restauration gâchent une partie de l’expérience et empêchent selon nous l’établissement d’être pleinement à la hauteur de son environnement exceptionnel.
Cela reste malgré tout un endroit magnifique et particulièrement adapté à une lune de miel. Dormir au milieu de l’océan, se réveiller avec cette vue et voir les tortues passer devant sa chambre est une expérience que nous n’oublierons pas ❤️🌴🐢🤿

Before getting to the Taaras, we had heard so many great things about the place. Even ChatGPT says it’s considered *the country’s* highest end hotel. We thought that was the reason why we were asked to pay 400€ per night (2 people room). If you have never traveled to Malaysia, you might not be aware of the currency value, so just know that an average meal for 2 is worth 100MYR (20€). Therefore you can only imagine how expensive this hotel is. Now, for this kind of money you really do expect the best of the best. Unfortunately, as you might have guessed already, that’s not the case. This was quite literally the worst hotel we’ve stayed at since we landed in Malaysia. Besides the staff being very kind, although most of the times you feel the service doesn’t reach the luxury they promise, and the private beach being objectively beautiful, the rest is honestly terrible. The rooms are big, yes, but super dark and old - in fact, the furniture must have stayed the same since the resort opened in 1996. 2 out of the 3 restaurants available in the resort are quite bad both aesthetically and food wise. The Italian/Indian one is ok, but we spent 450MYR (90€) for 2 mains and 1 plate of fruit, so also not great. The pool is always dirty and infested by kids. The resort also offers “complimentary” activities - too bad we wanted to rent gear for SUP and they answered it was already taken - wasn’t aware 5 star hotels only owned 1 paddle surf. We also spent 180MYR (40€) for a snorkeling activity, which was basically right beside the beach, so we could have just swum to the snorkeling location, and without the other 15 people that were with us. As mentioned, the beach is really nice, white sands, pristine water - all great. Too bad the sun beds are as decadent as the rest of the resort, plus there’s a big unbalance between the number of beds and the amount of guests the complex can host. Overall, a terrible experience very much misaligned with the price you pay.

I recently spent 3 nights at Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort, and unfortunately, it was a major disappointment. While the location is naturally beautiful, the resort’s management and operations are overwhelmingly biased toward a specific demographic, leaving international travelers in the dark and ignoring basic environmental ethics.
Communication & Service Gaps
The resort feels entirely geared toward mainland Chinese tourists, to the point where English-speaking guests are treated as an afterthought.
• The Briefing: Our "welcome briefing" in English lasted a mere 2 minutes and lacked vital information. Meanwhile, the Chinese-language briefing went on for 20 minutes. We missed out on key details, such as the option to visit neighboring islands to purchase fresh seafood to bring back.
• Logistics: Announcements are a struggle. When calling room numbers for boat departures or activities, staff used Chinese numbers only. Despite my name being clearly English on the manifest, I had to guess when they were referring to me.
• Payments: Even the bar is restrictive. They  accept QR code payments designed for mainland Chinese users, no acceptance of international credit cards or cash.
Environmental & Diving Concerns
This was the most upsetting part of the stay. For a resort located in such a delicate marine ecosystem, the lack of oversight is appalling.
• Wildlife Harassment: I witnessed guests (specifically from the majority group) petting and harassing sea turtles. Despite reporting this to the staff multiple times, zero action was taken.
• Poor Diving Standards: Many of the divers currently visiting appear to be unqualified or poorly trained. I saw constant reef damage—divers kicking the coral, touching marine life, and poking animals for photos.
• Staff Negligence: The dive guides and resort staff seem to prioritize guest "satisfaction" (allowing them to do whatever they want) over the protection of the reef.
Final Verdict
If you are an English speaker or a diver who cares about marine conservation and reef etiquette, stay elsewhere. The blatant disregard for environmental rules and the massive language barrier in service makes this resort a poor choice for global travelers. There are far better options in the Semporna area that respect both their guests and the ocean.

This is my first time staying at Berjaya Tioman Resort. I have been to Tioman Island numerous times, and always thought Berjaya Tioman Resort is such a high-end resort at Tioman island, and the resort must be of very high quality. However, after the stay at Berjaya, my impression had changed drastically.

The room condition is generally acceptable. The room comes with all the basic necessities. But, when we checked in, to our surprise, toilet roll was not provided! We had to ask for it. That is just tip of the iceberg. Then, here came the housekeeping with 1 roll of toilet roll! My friend was even joking, 'that's very generous of Berjaya"! We managed to get another extra one after asking for it.

The room sound proof is so bad that I could literally hear conversation from the next door! Our room was just separated by a door, and sound from next door can be easily audible from our room, especially kids crying/shouting!

The property is huge. There is buggy service to move guests around. But, the waiting time for the buggy pick-up is ridiculously long! On average, a 20 to 30 min waiting time is needed. We were told that there are only 2 buggies available for the whole facility (not sure how true it is), it is not sufficient to support the guest groups especially during peak period.

First time, we waited at the Main Gate for 30 mins for buggy to come.
Second time, we waited at our room for Buggy to pick up, and eventually we decided to just walk.
Third time, again we waited at the Main Gate for >20 mins for buggy under the hot sun (luckily the security guard offered us their chairs to sit)
Forth time, we waited at our room for buggy, and decided to walk to reception since we had to depart for ferry!

The worst is, we called for buggy pick-up and waited >30mins. Hence, we decided to just walk to the reception. My friend and I almost fainted to notice that, there was one buggy resting at the reception and no one bothered to drive the buggy for us!

The only plus point is the buggy staff is generally cheerful, helpful and polite.

To go outside of the facility (to the village), you have to pay additional RM50 per car (2-way)! Such a prestigious resort could have provided service to send guests to outside the property if required, not to mention that the food quality provided is sub-standard, and guests have to pay extra money if they want to opt for alternatives (out of Berjaya).

Berjaya has always known to be prestigious name in the industry, but Berjaya Tioman is far from a 4-star certified hotel. I would choose the budget homestay at Kampung Tekek over Berjaya considering the amount of money I had paid for the room!

Staying at Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort truly felt like disconnecting from everyday life. The resort is built over the sea, surrounded by water in every direction, with a very peaceful atmosphere. Sunrises and sunsets are beautiful, and at night you only hear the sound of the ocean — perfect for relaxing and relieving stress.

Diving is definitely the highlight. The nearby dive sites around Kapalai are rich in macro marine life, and the dive guides are professional and patient, always taking time to point out small creatures. Even for non-expert divers, the experience feels safe and enjoyable. The schedule is well-paced and not rushed.

The water villas are simple but comfortable, clean, with good air conditioning and comfortable beds. WiFi is limited, but that actually helps you unplug and fully relax.

Food options are not extensive, but meals are fresh and satisfying, especially after diving.
Overall, this is not a resort for nightlife or entertainment, but if you come for diving and true relaxation, Sipadan Kapalai is absolutely worth it.

Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort was truly one of the most unforgettable travel experiences of my life. If you love the ocean, nature, and marine life, this place is an absolute dream come true. Everything about the resort — from the location to the scenery to the water activities — feels like a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

The moment you arrive, you’ll be amazed by how beautiful Kapalai is. The waters are unbelievably clear, with stunning shades of blue and turquoise that you usually only see in photos. The resort sits on stilts above the sea, and the whole environment feels peaceful, private, and close to nature. Waking up to the sound of the ocean and seeing the sunrise over the water is something I will never forget.

What made this trip extra special for me is that I managed to snorkel and dive for the first time here. It was such a memorable and exciting experience! I was a bit nervous at the beginning, but the team guided me well and made me feel safe and confident. Snorkeling in Kapalai was already amazing — the visibility is so clear that you can see colourful fish, coral, and marine life easily, even near the resort area. It felt like entering a totally different world under the sea.

And the diving experience… wow. It was truly breathtaking. For a first-timer, this was the perfect place because the water is calm, crystal clear, and filled with marine life. Overall, Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort is a place I would highly recommend to anyone. Even if you’ve never snorkeled or dived before (like me), this is the perfect location to try — it’s safe, exciting, and absolutely unforgettable. We spent our anniversary at The Taaras Beach & Spa Resort and had an amazing experience overall. This was already our fifth stay at this beautiful resort, which says a lot about how much we enjoy this special place.

The location is truly a gem — the bay is stunning, the beach remains one of the most beautiful in Malaysia, and the staff are exceptionally friendly and welcoming. We will definitely return again.

That said, there are a few areas that deserve attention and improvement.

The general condition of the resort shows signs of aging and a major renovation is becoming necessary. The old roofing with visible discoloration gives parts of the resort an outdated feeling. The pool area also needs refurbishment, especially the bridge near the pool, which looks worn and old. A general revamp would greatly elevate the overall luxury experience.

The location alone cannot guarantee long-term success if maintenance and modernization are not prioritized. Considering the room rates range between RM2,500 and RM4,500 per night — making Taaras one of the most expensive resorts in Malaysia — guest expectations are naturally very high.

For these prices, I expected more attention to detail, especially regarding food and beverage quality. Breakfast should include genuinely fresh-squeezed orange juice, not artificial juice labeled as “fresh.” Small upgrades can make a huge difference in perceived luxury. Offering Prosecco at breakfast, as commonly found in many European 5-star hotels, would also elevate the experience significantly. If the resort wants to compete in the “Champions League” of luxury hospitality, serving cordial drinks at breakfast should be reconsidered.

We booked a cliff suite for two nights. I’ll start with the positives - the view is nice and the water is blue and clear. The staff are friendly.

Now for the negatives:

We arrived to a chaotic reception and waited for a few hours for our room (257) to be ready. After we were told by the reception desk that our room wasn’t ready we gathered our belongings in the reception where we were immediately pounced on by the spa manager who handed each of us a treatment menu and stood over us while we looked at it. After we declined, we waited on sun loungers on the beach. There is a buzzer to the bar to order drinks - we buzzed and someone came after about 20 minutes. No urgency, definitely no luxury. Sitting by the pool wasn’t an option as there wasn’t anywhere inviting to sit. Even if there was, the loungers face into the main hotel restaurant (why?) and the pool is not nice to look at.

When our room was ready we went back through to reception - which was still chaotic and loud - we were loaded onto a buggy with other families and taken to our room. It felt more like a cattle lorry than a 5* resort buggy. The reception staff also informed us that we would need to turn on the hot water 10-15 minutes before using the shower, which was surprising for a resort of this alleged ‘quality’.

Upon entering our room we were hit by a really foul smell. There were hairs on the floor and in the sink, and stains on the pillows and bed sheets. We told the reception desk that we were going for lunch and requested that housekeeping return to the room.

We ate lunch at the Asean restaurant. We both ordered king prawn fried rice which arrived without the prawns and was clearly cooked in dirty old oil. This cost £25. We didn’t return. There were screens all around the restaurant and in reception advertising activities turtle hatching (which wasn’t really what I wanted to watch while eating) - very tacky.

We went back to our room which had been re-cleaned but still had a foul smell. Everything looks tired and dirty. We saw monkeys riffling through (clean) bed sheets and towels, so it’s no wonder. Our towels had brown marks on them and need replacing desperately. The water pressure in the room was terrible, and the air con units urgently require replacing (along with everything else). It’s hard to articulate but it really just felt like a budget hotel.

At this stage we informed the front desk that we would be checking out the following morning and we made new travel arrangements. They offered to upgrade our room but we had seen enough (I think we had booked the most superior room type anyway) so politely declined. We ate dinner at a restaurant just outside the resort called Aima Grill Fish Restaurant (unconnected to the hotel) which was far better than the food we ate at lunchtime. We skipped breakfast and left the next morning. We have never left a hotel early before. They offered to refund the second night - I’ll update this review if the refund doesn’t end up materialising.

Although the view from our room was nice, having been on the beach we had seen quite a lot of rubbish both in the sand and the sea. In particular we noticed that the staff who stand near the towel counter leave their cigarette butts in the sand (when there is a bin close by) which explains why they are all over the beach. There is also a problem with sand flies - other people were covered in bites and there were notices about the sand flies on the beach and in our room.

Everything is either old, tired, broken or a combination of these things. I’m not entirely sure where the money is spent (our 2N stay cost nearly RM5800) but it is most certainly not on the hotel, hygiene or the guest experience. It is so gross.

At best this is a 2* resort masquerading as a luxury hotel. It is a complete rip off and we will never return or recommend it to anyone.

The garden suites, and if you want the most privacy possible, as for an upper level suite in a corner / end of row unit, away from heavy foot traffic.  To be honest and having stayed in many luxury resorts, I would say that this place is a little over priced, but there isn't a better resort on the island, so you are basically paying for their exclusivity, which they can charge as they deem fit as there's no direct competitor.

The staff were amazing, always willing to help with your needs and unlike many other hotels and resorts, they respond to any issues very promptly. You get assigned a personal concierge, who is but phone call or WhatsApp text away.

My friends and I stayed at Kapalai Resort for 4D3N in Dec 2023. The resort is entirely built on coral reefs and the accommodation is individual wooden chalet with ample privacy. I had a total of 9 dives around Mabul and Kapalai islands with 2 dives at nearby Sipadan island. Our best dives were at Sipadan Island where we saw tons of marine lives and a large school of Jacks. Snorkeling around Kapalai resort is accessible to many marine lives including the Hawksbill sea turtle. Sunset and sunrise were magnificent sights from the resort which provide great opportunity for photos shoot. The staffs on the resort are friendly and helpful and the amenities are adequate. However you may want to bring your own alcoholic drinks and snacks if you want to save some money. Meals are provided on the resort but limited to local dishes. However you have a choice to purchase seafood from the nearby Mabul island and the kitchen on the resort will be happy to cook them for  a small charge. We initially had a group of 4 but two of our friends had to cancel at the last minute due to medical and family emergencies. Kapalai resort could not offer a full refund but instead offered a change of date within 12 months from the initial date. Reason for rating 3 stars for service is because our booking was made through Kapalai Resort's agent Asia Dive Holidays (ADH) in KK and when we tried to reach ADH on WhatsApp to inform them of the emergency cancellation and refund, they were non-responsive and offered no assitance to us. We would not recommend Asia Dive Holidays for anyone looking at going to Kapalai resort or surrounding islands. We would also like Kapalai resort to review their partnership with Asia Dive Holidays and address the concerns we have regarding their unprofessionalism attitude and lousy customer service we received in our booking.

Unfortunately, this was one of the most disappointing marine parks I’ve visited. We came here for snorkeling and an introductory dive expecting a beautiful, protected marine environment, but instead, large parts of the experience genuinely felt like swimming in a landfill.

There was an unbelievable amount of plastic and other waste both in the water and along the beach. While swimming, it was almost impossible not to encounter plastic bottles, bags, and other pieces of trash, sometimes even getting caught in your hair. I understand that currents can bring large amounts of waste into the area and that this is not necessarily something the park can prevent. However, what I cannot understand is how there seems to be so little organized effort to regularly remove it, especially from a place designated as a marine park and visited by tour boats every day. Everyone behaved as if this were completely normal and simply an everyday occurrence.

A French tourist family eventually took it upon themselves to start cleaning the beach and filled what looked like around 30 baskets with garbage. Seeing visitors taking responsibility for cleaning a marine park while people working there (mostly tour guides/divers)
carried on as normal was honestly quite shocking.

As for the marine life, we did see plenty of fish, which was nice, but unfortunately, most of the coral appeared to be dead or severely damaged. Considering this is a protected marine park, I expected a much healthier and more vibrant underwater ecosystem.

I really hope more is done to protect and maintain this place. If currents regularly bring this much waste here, then regular cleanups, collecting floating waste with nets, and better coordination with the tour operators visiting every day seem desperately needed. A marine park should be a place where marine ecosystems are actively protected, not somewhere visitors have to swim through plastic waste.

It was genuinely sad to see.

"3D CVzion merujuk kepada gabungan konsep Computer Vision dengan elemen visualisasi tiga dimensi (3D) yang digunakan bagi menghasilkan persekitaran maya yang lebih realistik dan interaktif. Dalam konteks kajian Pemvisualan Kreatif Marin Laut menerusi Animasi 3D, 3D -CVzion berfungsi sebagai pendekatan kreatif untuk menterjemahkan data marin, seperti bentuk terumbu karang, spesies ikan, serta suasana dasar laut, ke dalam bentuk animasi yang lebih meyakinkan dan mudah difahami oleh khalayak.Subjek dan rujukan visual dalam kajian ini diperoleh secara langsung melalui aktiviti selaman di Pulau Payar. Melalui teknologi ini, pengalaman visual dapat ditingkatkan kerana penonton bukan sahaja melihat bentuk dan warna, tetapi juga dapat membayangkan kedalaman, perspektif, serta gerakan yang hampir menyerupai keadaan sebenar di bawah laut."

Manual untuk akses 3D -CVzion :
1.Buka kamera telefon pintar anda dan imbas kod QR yang disediakan.

2.Setelah berjaya diimbas, anda akan dibawa ke laman sesawang. Tekan butang Launch untuk membuka aplikasi.

3.Apabila paparan dibuka, logo 3D-CVzion akan muncul. Tekan logo tersebut untuk masuk ke halaman AR.

4.Gunakan kamera telefon pintar anda untuk mengimbas trigger image (contoh: gambar yang dipaparkan) dan nikmati pengalaman animasi 3D marin secara interaktif.

5.Selepas selesai, anda boleh kembali ke halaman informasi subjek untuk maklumat lanjut.

We had a great experience at Pulau Payar. I was a little hesitant to go because I couldn’t find a lot of recent reviews. But I’m glad we booked a trip here. I imagine it’s a much better experience now that they limit the number of visitors per day to 100. That being the case, you need to book ahead of time to make sure you get a spot. (Bookings open around 1 month prior to scheduled visit.)

We did the “Intro Dive” package, which includes an assisted 30 minute scuba dive, limited depth, followed by snorkeling. As we had never scuba dived before (and had no certification), this was perfect for us to try out scuba. We really enjoyed it and have a good idea now if we want to pursue certification or not. A master diver will stay with you the whole time. After the dive, we were able to snorkel the rest of the time. I found the visibility to be pretty good and there were some nice coral formations and a good variety of fish. We saw a lot of colorful fish (parrot fish and others), some squid, an eel, and a few puffer fish (some really big ones too!) to name a few highlights.

Our day looked like this:
Met at the Scuba Club at 8:30am to register, try on gear, etc. Got on the boat a little after 9am and took the 1 hr-long, fast, bumpy, wet ride to Pulau Payar. Because we were doing the intro dive, we were on a boat with other scuba divers, while another boat took snorkelers only. So I can’t really comment on what the snorkelers in the other boat did. We went to a site off of the main island and did our dive. Then we snorkeled around while the others continued their dives. We had lunch on the boat (simple chicken and rice dish), then went to another site. After the divers got off the boat in deeper water, then boat took us to the shallower water for us to snorkel. There was a beach there also where we could relax. But most of the time we stayed in the water. After an hour or so, we got back on the boat and headed back to Langkawi. We arrived back, changed clothes and turned in our wet suits.

There’s limited places to change clothes. Either you have to use a small bathroom or a storage closet area. But it’s essential you change into dry clothes if you’re looking to take a Grab from there. In fact, they told us to walk away from the Scuba Club a little ways before ordering the Grab, otherwise they won’t pick you up because they assume you are wet.

Shout out to Hello Langkawi and staff members Maui (Aoi) and Nasi. They took good care of us.
