Overall Impression
Except for the view, everything else fell far below expectations. I paid nearly RM6,000 for 2 nights, but the stay was nowhere near worth the price. This is not a 5-star resort—it is closer to 3-star. The property relies solely on its location while neglecting service, facilities, and maintenance. Unfortunately, other guests have raised similar issues in past reviews, and it is clear that no real improvements have been made.

Ratings
•	Price/Value: 2/5
•	Scenery & Location: 4/5
•	Facilities: 2/5
•	Access: 2/5
•	Service Quality: 2/5
•	Dining: 1/5
•	Cleanliness: 3/5

Beach & Location
The white sand beach was beautiful, clean, and well maintained. The view from the Cliff Bayview Suite was stunning. On this point alone, the resort deserves 5/5.

Room & Facilities
The suite was poorly maintained: TVs did not work, the air conditioner was broken, the floors felt gritty, and the bed mattress was uncomfortably hard. Bathwater was yellowish and cloudy, and tap water had a strong unpleasant smell. In-room dining dishes were left in the hallway for over two days. The bathroom amenities (L’Occitane) had an overly strong, chemical scent.
There were also two large flies inside the room, which gave a very unclean.This did not feel like a 5-star resort.

Check-in / Check-out & Service
While early check-in was allowed, overall service was unfriendly and mechanical. The welcome drink was handed out carelessly. The check-in process was rushed, with no explanation of facilities or activities. At check-out, staff simply processed the paperwork with no smile, no feedback, and no hospitality.

Dining
Breakfast was poor: hot dishes were already cold, the selection was limited, and seasoning was extreme. Complimentary soft drinks were only high-sugar choices (Fanta, A&W, Coke). Overall, the food quality was closer to 3-star level.

Activities
The snorkeling tour was disappointing: many corals were bleached, fish variety was low, and the sea was overcrowded with tours from the nearby public beach.

Other Issues
Wi-Fi did not work. Hot water took over 15 minutes to arrive and quickly turned cold. Guests had to set up their own sun loungers and collect towels from the counter. No complimentary water was provided.

Access
The resort is difficult to reach: 1-hour flight from Kuala Lumpur to Kuala Terengganu, another 1-hour drive to the jetty, and then a 40-minute boat ride. For international travelers, it is a long journey with little reward.

The services provided were excellent — from the sunbeds and umbrellas on the beach to the wide range of activities and excursions, everything was well organized and enjoyable. The breakfast buffet was rich and offered a great selection of international options, while lunch and dinner at the resort’s various restaurants were consistently delicious.

What really stood out to me was the service: the staff were exceptional — attentive, kind, and always eager to make guests feel comfortable. The cleanliness of the rooms was also impressive and contributed to an overall sense of care and attention to detail.

Overall, it’s a wonderful destination for anyone seeking relaxation, great service, and unforgettable experiences. I would definitely recommend it and would love to return.

L’hotel gode di una posizione spettacolare, immerso nella natura e affacciato direttamente sulla baia di Redang, un vero angolo di mondo che sembra dipinto. Abbiamo soggiornato in una suite Cliff Bay, prenotata su Booking, che ci ha lasciati senza parole: una camera enorme e luminosa, con terrazzino privato e vasca idromassaggio fronte mare da cui ammirare albe e tramonti indimenticabili. Il letto comodissimo, la cabina armadio spaziosa e il bagno con kit di prodotti Occitane completavano un ambiente curato nei minimi dettagli. La pulizia era impeccabile e ogni sera ci facevano trovare dei cioccolatini in camera, un pensiero semplice ma molto raffinato che ci ha fatto sentire coccolati.

Per raggiungere la suite, situata in posizione panoramica, bastava richiedere alla reception una delle macchinette elettriche che ci accompagnavano comodamente su e giù, un servizio rapido ed efficiente che abbiamo trovato davvero pratico.

La spiaggia privata è un vero gioiello: sabbia finissima che sembra borotalco, mare trasparente e lettini molto confortevoli. Un consiglio? Svegliarsi presto, verso le 7, per accaparrarsi la prima fila e vivere tutta la giornata con la baia davanti, senza nessun ostacolo alla vista.

Un’esperienza che rende Redang unica al mondo è la possibilità di nuotare con le tartarughe marine adulte nel loro habitat naturale e, in certi periodi, assistere al rilascio dei piccoli direttamente dalla spiaggia: un’emozione che resterà impressa nella memoria di grandi e bambini. Molto suggestiva anche l’escursione di snorkeling nella baia vicina, popolata da una miriade di pesci colorati.

La colazione era ricca e variegata, con opzioni internazionali e locali. Per i pasti ci siamo spesso fermati al The Cove, il bar-ristorante sulla spiaggia: atmosfera rilassata, piatti gustosi e prezzi corretti (una margherita o un hamburger circa 12 €). Cenare con la brezza marina e il suono delle onde in sottofondo è stata un’esperienza che da sola valeva il viaggio.

Il personale è stato sempre estremamente gentile e disponibile, pronto a soddisfare ogni esigenza con il sorriso, contribuendo a rendere il soggiorno ancora più piacevole.un ringraziamento  speciale al referente Hamdan che si è reso sempre attento e disponibile per darmi consigli e farci sentire a nostro agio!

Abbiamo trascorso quattro notti indimenticabili, ma la sensazione, al momento della partenza, era quella di non voler andare più via. Siamo stati ad agosto il tempo è stato sempre perfetto per godersi il mare e le attività all’aperto.

Che dire: soldi spesi benissimo, un luogo che rimane nel cuore… ci tornerei domani stesso!

Ho trascorso un soggiorno splendido al Taras Resort di Redang, un’esperienza che merita pienamente 5 stelle.

La cosa che mi è piaciuta di più è stata la spiaggia privata: tranquilla, curata e con un mare spettacolare.
Nuotando, si può raggiungere facilmente il Turtle Point e nuotare insieme alle tartarughe, un’emozione unica.
I lettini sono ben posizionati e il servizio in spiaggia è eccellente: ti portano tutto quello che desideri, creando un’atmosfera di relax totale.

Un altro punto forte sono i servizi inclusi: yoga al mattino e al pomeriggio, una palestra meravigliosa con vista sull’oceano, kayak, biliardo, ping-pong serale, karaoke room… anche restando in hotel per più giorni senza fare escursioni, ci sono tantissime attività per non annoiarsi mai.

Le camere sono belle e confortevoli. Consiglio quelle con garden view o ocean view, che hanno la posizione migliore. Quelle con vista collina richiedono di prendere un transfer o fare parecchie scale, quindi sono da valutare in base alle preferenze e al budget.

Sul fronte ristorazione, l’hotel è pensato principalmente per un pubblico asiatico, quindi il buffet è ricco di piatti tipici locali (molto buoni: il roti e le uova scramble erano ottimi).
C’è anche un ristorante vicino alla spiaggia per la cena, buono ma non eccezionale, e un bar fronte mare meraviglioso, dove mangiare hamburger, pizza e drink con una vista incredibile.

Unica pecca per chi, come noi, viaggia senza bambini: ci sono molti gonfiabili e giochi sparsi per l’hotel, quindi capita di sorseggiare un aperitivo con bambini che saltano accanto. Sarebbe ideale creare una zona dedicata solo ai piccoli. Le piscine, spesso piene di bambini e di ospiti che fanno il bagno vestiti, risultano meno godibili. Inoltre, le nuove costruzioni di camere stanno un po’ rovinando il paesaggio.

In sintesi: un resort con mare da cartolina, tantissime attività e relax assicurato, perfetto per famiglie e coppie che cercano servizi e comfort. Qualche dettaglio migliorabile, ma l’esperienza complessiva è stata davvero bellissima

We stayed here for 3 days and 2 nights (Monday to Wednesday in July). A day before our arrival, we called the hotel to inform them of our ferry arrival time. On the day itself, we were warmly welcomed by the hotel’s shuttle van driver as soon as we arrived. At check-in, we were greeted by a cheerful receptionist and offered a refreshing welcome drink - perfect for the warm weather.

We checked into our Garden Suite shortly after. The room was clean, comfortable, and inviting. We quickly brewed the complimentary coffee capsules provided in the room to recharge before exploring the hotel grounds and heading to the beach.

The beach was stunning - clean with soft white sand and peaceful, as it wasn’t crowded during our stay. We tried kayaking for the first time, which turned out to be a fun and enlightening experience. The next morning, we joined the 8 AM guided nature walk - a nice bit of exercise, especially for those of us used to sitting behind a laptop. The guides were friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable throughout.

During our stay, we enjoyed breakfast at the Asean All-Day Dining restaurant on both mornings. The buffet spread had plenty of choices - enough to spoil any appetite. The atmosphere at the resort was lovely, and the staff were consistently cheerful and accommodating.

For those using Maxis/Hotlink, signal coverage is strong throughout the resort. I had planned to get some work done - but with a beach that tempting, it was impossible to resist relaxing instead.

The beautiful weather, powdery sand, and turquoise-blue sea felt almost surreal - like stepping into a painting. We also explored Turtle Beach, which is just a short walk from the resort’s private beach. It was a fun little adventure.

A big thank you to all the amazing staff here - the drivers, the receptionists, the lifeguards, the snorkeling guides, the room service team, and everyone else who made our stay so memorable.

We only wish the trip could have been longer. We’d definitely love to return!

7th to 13th of July 2025, What I appreciated most was the stunning white sandy beach and the spacious room with effortless beach access, which made things much easier while traveling with my one-year-old baby. A special mention goes to Hamdan, the room service assistant, whose kindness and attentiveness throughout my six-night stay at The Taaras truly stood out. The staff overall were warm and courteous, though I believe a touch more professional training would help meet the refined standards expected of a five-star resort. Among the dining experiences, both ASEAN and Merenero restaurant teams were welcoming, yet Merenero’s staff demonstrated a noticeably higher level of attentiveness. One memorable gesture was when I found myself without cash while waiting for the boat transfer—one of the staff not only guided me to the nearest ATM but personally took me there on his scooter, an act of genuine hospitality I won’t forget. On the less favorable side, the room furnishings felt outdated, with noticeable gaps that allowed lizards inside during my stay, and the towels were worn and rough on the skin. Breakfast lacked variety, leaving the experience feeling repetitive. Adding to that, aside from Hamdan, staff professionalism could be elevated; starting from Merang Jetty where I noticed staff smoking in the waiting area despite the presence of my baby, which felt far from appropriate. This was not a gesture of goodwill, but simply the minimum necessary response. At the same time, I was told that no responsible person was available to make any decisions regarding compensation and that I should follow up by email. We stayed 6 nights and 7 days at this fantastic resort. I would like to share my experience so that those who choose this resort are aware of the significant limitations that unfortunately this magnificent structure presents.

Value for money 5/10
Considering a cost of about 650 euros per night for two people (High season - diving package with 3 or 4 dives per day), I wouldn't return to this resort.

The company policy is mainly oriented on the Asian market, and this choice affects numerous aspects that I will list here:

1. The transfer by speedboat from Semporna Port to Kapalai was not at all comfortable. We are used to the sea, and I understand that the weather conditions cannot be controlled, and there is an internal schedule to follow. However, I would like to emphasize that the boat was not suitable for those sea conditions; the rigid hull continuously slammed against the waves, resulting in a sore back. The captain could have easily reduced the speed.

2. Inadequate and unprepared staff. The management was careless in addressing various issues raised, and there was a total lack of authority in enforcing the necessary rules for civil coexistence and respect for this magnificent ecosystem and for those who wanted to spend relaxing moments.

2. Hygiene, cleanliness, and maintenance of the structure need improvement. The rooms are large and spacious with air conditioning, a fan, kettle, minibar, and safe, but a bit outdated. Maintenance is needed, especially in the bathroom. There are different types of chalets, some recently renovated. At the time of check-in, the room was very dirty, the wooden floor had not been cleaned, dust everywhere, especially on the shelves of the open wardrobe, and we even found a used soap in the shower. Towels were washed and fragrant but stained (despite being changed every day). Bird droppings on the balcony were not cleaned for days. Periodically, between 1:00 PM and 5:00 PM, maintenance workers start their work, and they don't care about the noise they make. The wooden planks of the pier that connect the rooms, since they are not properly fixed, make a terrible noise every time bicycles or golf carts pass near the room (this happens at all hours).

3. Environmental awareness and pollution control are non-existent. The showers in the rooms drain directly into the fantastic crystalline waters surrounding the resort, releasing polluting substances from the used soaps and organic waste (we even saw floating organic waste). Some areas of the resort's walkways are cleaned with bleach, which ends up directly in the sea after washing/rinsing.

4.Non-existent internet connection (this could be a plus for some). Wi-Fi is only available in the reception area, but it's very slow. Despite buying local SIM cards for data connection, the signal was completely absent for 2 days due to issues with the resort's receiver antenna
.
5. Good food for those who enjoy Asian cuisine. There is a total absence of continental dishes, only predominantly Asian cuisine with limited variety

Our dive guide, Wei, also collapsed the signal buoy after about 3 minutes, and I had to plead with him to put it back up because it was obvious the boat had not seen us. Fortunately, luck was on our side and the current was pushing us back to Kapalai, but we swam for an hour to make it back safely. This could have been catastrophic if not for the current and where our dive site was. The manager of the dive center was apathetic to the situation and just directed us to the manager of the resort. This was my second stay at the resort, and once again, I had a great experience. The location is excellent, with beautiful surroundings, and the staff were friendly and very helpful throughout our stay.The resort has two restaurants, although the Thai restaurant was closed during our visit. The Jetty Paya restaurant is just outside the main gate and can be easily reached by buggy. The Sarang Seafood restaurant is about 2 km from the resort, and a return taxi fare is around RM50.Snorkeling trips to Coral Island, Renggis Island, and the marine park, as well as taxi services for going to restaurants, can all be organized through the hotel. You can also visit the marine park by taxi (suitable if traveling with senior citizens), which costs around RM100–150. Activities within the resort includes a game zone for kids, gym, pool table (4RM per game), bicycling, and kayaking. We appreciated the complimentary 1-hour bicycle ride provided by the staff.Breakfast was decent, but it would be even better with a wider variety of options. The room includes all the necessary amenities, but could be more modernized to better match the overall resort experience. The resort provided a complimentary minibar in two of the three rooms we booked, which was a nice added touch.Overall, it was another enjoyable stay, and I would definitely consider coming back again.

Nous avions réservé 4 nuits au Perhentian Island Resort, mais nous avons dû quitter les lieux dès notre arrivée tant la chambre était dans un état inacceptable. Nous avons constaté la présence de cafards, de crottes supposées de souris, de moisissures, de toiles d’araignées, de poussière accumulée, ainsi que des murs tachés de sang d’insectes écrasés. Le sol était sale, et une forte odeur d’urine se dégageait du matelas.

Face à un tel manque d’hygiène, il était impensable d’y passer la nuit. Nous avons immédiatement décidé de partir et de séjourner au Marriott, qui était notre premier choix et qui, lui, offre un cadre irréprochable.

Je regrette d’avoir choisi cet établissement uniquement pour sa localisation, car il est tout à fait possible de profiter de la plage du PIR en séjournant dans un autre hôtel bien mieux entretenu et en s’y rendant simplement en taxi boat.

Ce qui est encore plus inacceptable, c’est l’absence totale de réponse de la part de la direction malgré nos nombreux mails concernant le remboursement des nuits non consommées. Ce silence en dit long sur le sérieux de la gestion et le respect accordé aux clients.

Je déconseille très fortement cet hôtel. Il ne mérite absolument pas sa réputation ni ses tarifs, et j’espère sincèrement que cet avis évitera à d’autres voyageurs la même mésaventure.

The architecture of the room was awesome in terms of vibes.

However, the cleanliness and maintenance of the room are way subpar. The room is also really outdated and poorly maintained. Given the room rate, we were expecting at the very least, a clean and well-maintained room.

Our stay at Perhentian Island Resort was generally relaxing, especially with the breathtaking sea view right from the room — the turquoise water and soft waves were simply mesmerizing. However, the cleanliness could use some serious improvement. The room was dusty, and the floor still had sand, which made it feel like it hadn’t been properly cleaned before check-in. While the receptionist (Adeena?) and housekeeping staff were polite and helpful, some of the other staff, especially in Restaurant, could benefit from proper training in hospitality and guest care. The restaurant food was just average — edible but not particularly memorable. Bihun sup was tasty, though.

Despite these downsides, the location and view make it worth visiting, especially for those who love nature and peaceful surroundings. With better upkeep and staff training, this resort could easily become one of the best stays on the island.

L’hôtel bénéficie d’un atout indéniable : son emplacement. Situé sur la plus belle plage des îles Perhentian, le cadre est tout simplement paradisiaque. Le snorkeling est fabuleux : nous avons eu la chance de nager avec plusieurs tortues, une raie et même des petits requins dès notre premier bain. Incroyable !

En revanche, l’hôtel en lui-même est vieillissant et le service n’est clairement pas à la hauteur. La porte des toilettes bloque l’ouverture de la salle de bain, aucun ménage n’a été fait dans les chambres pendant nos 3 jours de séjour, aucune serviette supplémentaire disponible sans supplément, et aucune vaisselle propre fournie : il fallait laver nous-mêmes les tasses et verres mis à disposition pour le thé et le café.

En résumé : un hôtel qui se repose entièrement sur son atout principal — une plage exceptionnelle — mais qui gagnerait énormément à améliorer la qualité de ses prestations.

Premetto che l’isola offre un panorama mozzafiato. Il mare è spettacolare con tutta la fauna marina che si può ammirare a pochi metri dalla riva. Detto questo, struttura, che dovrebbe essere la migliore e infatti è la più costosa, non è minimamente pronta ad accogliere turismo europeo. Cade letteralmente a pezzi, è sporca e abbandonata a se stessa. Le camere sono fatiscenti e con una scarsissima igiene. Lenzuola e asciugamani macchiati. Non è questione di sapersi adattare, perche quella non mi manca visti i molti viaggi in posti molto meno pretenziosi fatti negli anni scorsi. 40 gradi al sole e non si può bere una birra o qualsiasi tipo di alcolico da nessuna parte tranne in un bar gestito da personale cinese in un’altra spiaggia. La qualità del servizio è davvero pessimo. Merita venire solo per la spiaggia che è paradisiaca ma tre giorni sono più che sufficienti, se, lo ripeto, si possiede un grandissimo spirito di adattamento a sporcizia e odori. Peccato davvero perché avrebbe davvero grande potenziale vista la posizione. Infatti molti ospiti cambiano struttura non appena fatto il check-in. Ma essendomi informata credo che questa sia addirittura la migliore.

La première chambre était sale et vétuste coincée entre un marécage et la forêt tropicale tout au fond. On a demandé à changer. La deuxième proposée était tout aussi calamiteuse. J'ai donc cherché moi même sur internet et pu leur montrer qu'il y en avait une en première ligne de plage. Nous l'avons eue avec un surcout. Néanmoins hormis la plage en face du bungalow elle était vieille, abimée à refaire! Vu l'emplacement ils ont un potentiel de fou alors que tout est délabré. C'est à n'y rien comprendre. Le personnel se fiche de tout. Ils doivent être désabusés. Tout le monde qui arrive demande à changer. Personne n'est venu nous chercher à l'embarcadère alors qu'une personne à moto avec remorque est censé faire ce job. On a du transporté nos bagages sous un soleil de plomb. Tout l'hôtel est vieux. Les repas n'ont aucune saveur et les tables sont limites au niveau propreté. Seule la plage en face est magnifique. Sable blanc et eau translucide, tortues, bébé requins, poissons. Quel gâchis!

La ubicación y la playa delante del hotel es la MEJOR DE LA ISLA sin duda, esa es la parte positiva. Lo negativo:

1- El restaurante del hotel es MUY mejorable, los precios son un poco mas elevados que en otras zonas pero no pasaría absolutamente nada si la comida estuviera bien, pero es que no lo esta (a excepcion de algún plato concreto). Se nota que nadie controla nada y que no hay un jefe vigilando. El desayuno es básico pero correcto.

2- Las habitaciones SON LA PEOR PARTE, el mantenimiento de estas es NULO. Paredes, armarios, suelo todo desgastado y viejo. Si fuera solo eso, la puntuación sería mayor pero no, la LIMPIEZA DEBEN IMPLEMENTARLA, no hay mosquiteras en las camas, ayer por la noche tuvimos que matar sin exagerar 15 miniinsectos que no sé decir que eran, parecian minimosquitos. Teniendo en cuenta que lo hemos tenido todo siempre cerrado y cerrabamos la puerta enseguida, se entiende que estás en la selva y habra bichos pero no en tal cantidad, deben implementar medidas para que esto no pase, pagamos 113€ (por la habitación estándar, no cerca del mar) por noche, no 30€. Y bueno ya los que nos dejo boquiabiertos fue encontrar una especie de arenilla debajo de la cama en gran cantidad, tras investigar un poco parece que son excrementos de termita NO ESTOY SEGURA pero arena no era. En conclusión, no duermes agusto.

3- El servicio: si que es cierto nos encontramos personas agradables, había otras que no se caracterizaban por su amabilidad.

No se si es una situación aislada o no, ya que no hemos estado en otros hoteles de esta isla, no se si es frecuente pero estuvimos en Ombak Resort (en Kecil) y mucho mejor, tanto restaurante como las habitaciones y la atención.

La playa es un paraíso, pero el resort es un infierno.

Habitaciones sucias, sin limpieza real (solo cambian toallas, ni reponen papel higiénico ni agua), instalaciones viejas y llenas de humedad. El restaurante es caótico: no te atienden, la comida es pésima y cara, y no sirven alcohol (algo que no se avisa). El centro de buceo incapaz de ofrecer ni siquiera un instructor privado.

Terminamos salvando nuestras vacaciones en el resort vecino The Barat, donde sí nos atendieron bien y pude bucear con un instructor privado excelente.

Conclusión: este hotel vive solo de su ubicación. La playa es única, pero el “resort” está en estado de abandono y arruina la experiencia.

We stayed at Coral View Resort but often wandered over to the beach in front of Perhentian Island Resort, as it turned out to be one of the nicest stretches of sand in the area. The beach here is wider and more sandy compared to other spots, making it much more comfortable for relaxing, strolling, or just lying down under the sun. The water is usually clear and calm, which makes swimming and snorkeling very enjoyable. Right in front of the beach lies Turtle Point, one of the best places on the island to spot sea turtles. With just a short swim out, it’s quite common to encounter these gentle creatures gracefully gliding through the water, which makes the experience unforgettable.

The only downside is that it can get rather busy at times, as boats frequently stop to drop off groups of snorkelers, which slightly disturbs the otherwise peaceful setting. Still, once you’re in the water, the beauty beneath quickly makes up for it. When snorkeling, don’t just stay at Turtle Point—be sure to swim toward the rocky areas on both the left and right sides of the beach. There you’ll find an abundance of colorful fish, vibrant corals, and even black-tipped reef sharks cruising gracefully in the shallows.

Se definen como un hotel resort y lo único que son es un puñado de habitaciones viejas delante de una playa turquesa, con unos servicios absolutamente deplorables. Este lugar fue la mayor decepción de mi viaje.||La Ilusión de la Playa Paradisíaca||||A primera vista, la playa puede parecer un paraíso, pero la realidad es otra. A pesar de tener agua turquesa, el entorno marino es una completa decepción. No hay arrecife de coral vivo; todo es arena de coral muerto sin apenas peces a la vista. Si buscas hacer snorkel o bucear, tienes que nadar a una profundidad extrema para, con suerte, encontrar una tortuga.||||Habitaciones y Mantenimiento: Viejas y Sucias||Las habitaciones son viejas y están en un estado de abandono total, y nada justifica el precio. La limpieza es inexistente: el personal no repuso el papel higiénico y las condiciones de la habitación eran inaceptables. En el baño encontramos moho en las juntas y grifos llenos de cal, además de manchas de humedad en el techo. Fuera, el panorama era desolador, con montones de basura y escombros acumulados por el lugar.||||Servicios: Inexistentes y Decepcionantes||El servicio, en general, es pésimo. El personal de recepción es poco amable y no da información. Pero lo más grave fue el centro de buceo, que era una de las razones principales para nuestra visita. Fuimos a preguntar para reservar un día privado y dos inmersiones, y simplemente nos dijeron que no era posible, lo que arruinó la experiencia.||||La Comida: Un Auténtico Fraude||El restaurante es un capítulo aparte. El buffet del desayuno es pobre y limitado, y la comida es tan mala que tuvimos que ir a comer a restaurantes cercanos. Los precios son desorbitados para la bajísima calidad que ofrecen. Además, para los futuros huéspedes, es importante saber que el hotel no sirve bebidas alcohólicas.||Conclusión||||No te dejes engañar por el título de "resort". Este lugar carece de todo lo que promete: ni limpieza, ni buen servicio, ni buena comida, ni un arrecife vivo. Si valoras una experiencia de calidad, te recomiendo encarecidamente que busques otro hotel.

Resort situato sull'isola besar "isola grande". Un Resort tranquillo dove hai la possibilità di goderti di una vacanza relax. Nei pressi del Resort hai la possibilità di spostarti a piedi e raggiungere altri due Resort dove poter mangiare e farsi il bagno, oppure dal tuo Resort utilizzare i taxi boat per raggiungere altre spiagge o l'isola kecil dove troverai più movida. Abbiamo scelto una superior class twin e invece ci è stato assegnato una camera standard in un bungalow di legno. Pulizia nei minimi dettagli sia a livello di asciugamani che lenzuola. I bungalow sono immersi nella natura quindi puoi trovare o sentire animaletti. Colazione a buffet con ampia scelta, mentre per pranzo e cena ti danno la possibilità di scegliere tra buffet o alla carte. Il Resort dispone di spiaggia con ombrelloni e sdraio privati.

If we could rate this resort higher than 5 stars, we absolutely would. After a long journey, our first experience at another place, Fauna Beach Resort, was so miserable and poorly maintained that we immediately started looking for an alternative. Thankfully, for a bit more money, we were able to book a stay at Perhentian Island Resort, and it turned out to be the best decision we made on our entire long vacation.

You have to remember that this is an island, and everything has to be brought in by boat, which makes the level of care and cleanliness at this resort truly remarkable. There are no highways, landfills, or hardware stores, yet they manage to keep everything in pristine condition.

This resort is absolutely fantastic and cared for down to the last detail. The breakfast was great, the rooms were clean and cool with air conditioning, and we received fresh water and towels every single day. The private beach with comfortable sunbeds is located right next to Turtle Beach, one of the most famous snorkeling spots on the Perhentian Islands.
Within walking distance is the wonderful restaurant The Barat, which offers delicious and affordable food. Unlike the resort's restaurant, they also serve a variety of beers, which was a nice bonus.

All in all, this was a fantastic experience. We would recommend anyone to spend a little more for this kind of luxury. The (slightly) cheaper Fauna Beach Resort was twenty times worse and practically falling apart. Count your blessings and go to Perhentian Island Resort; it’s worth every single euro!

Solid dive resort with an onsite dive shop and genuinely wonderful staff. The beach was beautiful, the water crystal clear, and I even saw baby black tip sharks in the shallows (harmless and amazing to see).

Chalets were comfortable with good air-conditioning, but dated and in need of maintenance. Amenities are very basic, with only two small plastic bottles of water provided daily, no dispensers, and extras must be bought at the gift shop. It’s awful that water only comes in plastic bottles, especially when the beach is already littered with caps. I picked up two bucketfuls of plastic waste just walking along the shore.

The BBQ buffet was tasty but ran out quickly, while the regular buffet was limited and not always fresh.

Overall, a good dive base with a beautiful setting, though it was really sad to see both the coral bleaching and the amount of plastic waste.

Insomma… non ci sono parole 😅

The last resort|Unfortunately, I whole-heartedly agree with previous reviewers. There are only two factors that keep the resort going - the wonderful beach and sea access, and the fact that - at least during the current high season - the demand for rooms is such that even very over-rated (and over-paid) facilities like the PIR get filled.  It sort of becomes the 'last resort' for people like us who do not book super-early and so miss out on any of the chain of much better places (supposedly lower grade) on this larger of the two islands - including Coral View, Abdul's Chalet, Mama's, Tuna Bay and several others.  All markedly better in most respects than the Perhentian Island Resort.  The place visibly dates back to the 80s, and much of it has not been renovated / updated since then.  No need to repeat what others have said - but just a few examples of the many seemingly little things that 'irked' us.  Breakfast - buffet type, but with low quality products throughout - old (non-fresh) chewy 'croissants', low quality juices, really almost undrinkable coffee... large round tables with unironed table-cloth that still have food remnants from the night before.  No ROTI CANAI - which is a major product produced and consumed for breakfast at the other, smaller resorts. Service people stand in corners of the room but are not helpful at all (except when collecting the pointless breakfast vouchers..).  There is an espresso / coffee machine - but when you ask, any 'good coffee' costs extra (different from 4 star hotels elsewhere).  - Rooms: no hot water (not essential here, but nice to have - available in some of the 'lower grade' resorts nearby).  No TV (again, not essential - but the others have it). Rooms all need to be 'redone' as well as thoroughly cleaned. - Staff - many are friendly and helpful enough, but generally do not seem to be trained well, or speak enough English for this kind of place.  Management / supervision overall seems to be lacking.  Example: we finally moved out to another resort.  The front desk is asked to call the other resort to send a boat. Staff tries once to call, then turns to us and says: no one answering the phone.  We try and immediately get someone and so arrange it all ourselves. - Anyway - our bottom line, and recommendation would be for the owners to do 2 main things: 1) to close the entire place for an entire season (or whatever it takes) to do a major overhaul of the entire facility, and 2) equally important, to seriously strengthen management and supervision, as well as retrain staff.
